contested_upside.note: Excluded from saving_per_unit_usd on purpose. Each line is a part the carrier's design choice removes, where this repo's own sources disagree about whether the module build needed it. Settle them on a bench, then move them into `absorbs` or drop them — do not let them drift into the headline unresolved.

lines.claim: The PCB-antenna WROOM-1 variant needs no external whip, so a carrier build never buys one.
lines.dispute: docs/hardware/bom_canary_wap.csv marks ANT1 Optional and notes 'XIAO has onboard antenna.' firmware/boards/boards.json says of the same board: 'External u.FL antenna required — WiFi and BLE (pairing + offline console) need it seated; without it Bluetooth may not work at all.' Both cannot be true.
lines.how_to_settle_it: Bench, not documentation: run the WAP's BLE pairing and offline console on a Sense with the u.FL whip removed. Whichever way it goes, fix the loser — this contradiction misleads anyone buying parts today, independently of whether this board is ever built.

delta.breakeven_note: Units that must be built before the carrier has paid back its own NRE. It excludes certification entirely — the Part 15B SDoC in board.json `certification` is owed whether or not this board exists, because it attaches to shipping a radio, not to which PCB the radio sits on.

decision.why: 102010469 is priced at $15.90 at qty 1 (digikey), which cannot answer a 1000-unit question: that is a catalog price for one piece, not the price we would pay. Add a quote at qty 1000 to board.json `volume_quotes` and this becomes GO or STOP automatically.
decision.how_to_resolve: Cheapest first: (1) set MOUSER_API_KEY as an Actions secret — the nightly bom-pricing job then fetches Mouser's published breaks for a SKU it already resolves, and if those reach the basis volume the question answers itself with no human in the loop; (2) failing that, ask Seeed directly (they sell the XIAO and quote volume readily) for 100/500/1000 pricing on 102010469; (3) Digi-Key/Mouser will both quote a volume price on request even when they publish none. Any of the three lands as one row above.

sensitivity.question: How cheap would 102010469 have to get before this carrier stops paying for itself?
sensitivity.verdict: The carrier is cheaper while 102010469 costs more than $11.32/unit. It is modeled at $15.90 at qty 1. This is the number to re-check against a real volume quote before committing NRE — it needs no estimate to compute, only the price of one part.

confidence_accounting.note: Share of the compared dollars that a distributor actually resolved this snapshot, versus a human's stated estimate. Read the saving with this number next to it.

volume_mismatch.note: Lines the snapshot could only price below the 1000-unit basis. On the replaced side this OVERSTATES the saving (we credit ourselves a low-volume price for a part we are dropping); on the carrier side it understates it. Any line here is a volume quote waiting to be got.
